title: Test Your Understanding: Design a Notification System
description: Channels, queues, idempotency, and retry storms.

questions.question: Product services should typically trigger notifications by:

options.text: Calling SendGrid directly from the order API handler
Publishing domain events consumed by a notification service
Writing to the user's inbox synchronously in every service
Polling the database every second for changes

questions.explanation: Decouple with events + async workers — product APIs stay fast and notification logic stays centralized.

questions.question: An idempotency key for notifications often includes:

options.text: Only a random UUID per worker attempt
event_id, user_id, channel, and template version

questions.explanation: Stable key from business event + recipient + channel prevents duplicate sends on queue redelivery.

questions.question: Separate priority queues for transactional vs marketing notifications prevents:
questions.explanation: High-priority transactional traffic must not sit behind bulk marketing fan-out.

questions.question: On HTTP 429 from a push provider, workers should:

options.text: Retry immediately in a tight loop

questions.explanation: Rate limits require exponential backoff and token buckets — tight retries cause retry storms.

questions.question: Invalid device push tokens should:

options.text: Be removed from the user's device list on permanent provider error
Block all channels for the user

questions.explanation: Dead tokens waste QPS and fail every send — clean up on 400-class permanent errors.

questions.question: Quiet hours mean some notifications may be delayed until the user's local morning.
questions.explanation: Non-critical push can queue during quiet hours; transactional/critical may bypass per policy.

questions.question: What causes notification retry storms? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Re-enqueueing failed jobs with no backoff or dedup before send
Unique constraint on idempotency key before provider call
Unstable event_id changing on upstream retries

questions.explanation: Immediate retries + duplicate event IDs multiply sends. Dedup keys and backoff prevent storms.

questions.question: Broadcasting a campaign to 1M users resembles:

options.text: Feed fan-out — enqueue per-user jobs with rate-limited workers

questions.explanation: One event fans out to many recipients via queue — same amplification patterns as timeline push.
